title: Fix: Explicitly define `security` requirement for docs as per OpenAPI specification
description:
Fixes #90 

Currently, the way docs add the `security` requirement is as follows:

```r
self$add_api_doc(
  fp$flow_to_openapi(flow, auth_scope),
  subset = c("paths", as_openapi_path(path), method)
)
```

This fix proposes explicitly mentioning this so that doc providers pick it up.

```r
self$add_api_doc(
  list(security = fp$flow_to_openapi(flow, auth_scope)),
  subset = c("paths", as_openapi_path(path), method)
)
```

I've already tested this manually and it seems to solve the wall I was hitting in trying out `plumber2` for a while.

title: docs(vignettes): Expand on hosting vignette
description:
Fixes #15 
Related #60 

## Summary

This PR significantly expands the hosting guide for plumber2 APIs with comprehensive deployment options and best practices. The documentation now covers multiple hosting strategies from enterprise solutions to self-managed deployments, making it easier for users to choose and implement the right hosting approach for their needs.

## Changes

- **Expanded hosting guide** ([vignettes/hosting.qmd](vignettes/hosting.qmd)): Added detailed sections covering:
  - Enhanced `_server.yml` documentation with creation and testing examples
  - DigitalOcean deployment using the `buoyant` package
  - Docker containerization with example Dockerfile
  - Process management with pm2 (includes clustering, logging, and monitoring)
  - Native systemd service configuration for Linux servers
  
## Documentation Improvements

The hosting guide now provides:
- Step-by-step instructions for each deployment method
- Prerequisites and installation requirements
- Real-world code examples and configuration files
- Management commands for each hosting option
- Links to external resources and tools

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify all code examples in the hosting guide are valid
	* I have only confirmed buoyant and docker
	* I **will not** be testing the `systemd` or `pm2` sections. They seemed ok from a distance 🙃 
- [x] Test that the expanded documentation builds correctly
- [x] Confirm all external links are working


-----------------

Once the PR is merged, I'll send `{buoyant}` to CRAN 😃

title: `tags` argument is list in `openapi_operation()` rather than a character
description: Can be seen with: ``` library(plumber2) api_obj1 <- api(doc_type = "swagger", port = 8081) |> api_get( path = "sales", handler = identity, route = "ecommerce" ) |> api_doc_add( doc = openapi( info = openapi_info( title = "E-commerce API", version = "0.1.0", ), tags = list( openapi_tag(name = "ecommerce", description = "E-commerce data") ), paths = list( "sales" = openapi_path( "Conversion data", "Retrieve e-commerce conversion data", get = openapi_operation( tags = "ecommerce" # character makes path nesting badly rendered on swagger (one per character) ) ) ) ) ) api_run(api_obj1) api_obj2 <- api(doc_type = "swagger", port = 8082) |> api_get( path = "sales", handler = identity, route = "ecommerce" ) |> api_doc_add( doc = openapi( info = openapi_info( title = "E-commerce API", version = "0.1.0", ), tags = list( openapi_tag(name = "ecommerce", description = "E-commerce data") ), paths = list( "sales" = openapi_path( "Conversion data", "Retrieve e-commerce conversion data", get = openapi_operation( tags = list("ecommerce") # list ) ) ) ) ) api_run(api_obj2) ``` What I mean by badly rendered:

title: Fix pass tags argument in `openapi_operation()`
description:
Otherwise `tags` argument is not passed downstream:

``` r
library(plumber2)

openapi_operation(
  summary = "My summary",
  description = "My desc",
  operation_id = "opid",
  tags = "ecommerce"
)
#> $summary
#> [1] "My summary"
#> 
#> $description
#> [1] "My desc"
#> 
#> $operation_id
#> [1] "opid"
#> 
#> $response
#> list()
```

<sup>Created on 2025-05-20 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

With the fix, `tags` is in the output:

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading plumber2

openapi_operation(
  summary = "My summary",
  description = "My desc",
  operation_id = "opid",
  tags = "ecommerce" 
)
#> $summary
#> [1] "My summary"
#> 
#> $description
#> [1] "My desc"
#> 
#> $operation_id
#> [1] "opid"
#> 
#> $tags
#> [1] "ecommerce"
#> 
#> $response
#> list()
```

<sup>Created on 2025-05-20 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>
